label: TP
reason: Alert 1 (java/insecure-randomness): alert-TP — resolved sink value is rememberMeKey derived from Math.random(), used as cookie value and session attribute; Math.random() is predictable and inappropriate for security-sensitive tokens. Alert 2 (java/xss): alert-TP — resolved sink value is user-provided param from request header: valuesList starts as ['safe', param, 'moresafe'], remove(0) removes 'safe', then get(0) retrieves param directly; param flows to response.getWriter() without HTML encoding. Both alerts represent real vulnerabilities.

evidence.note: Math.random() generates insecure randomness for rememberMeKey used in cookies/sessions
XSS path: param from header -> valuesList[0] after remove(0) -> response.getWriter() without encoding
Sink writes user input to HTML response without HTML entity encoding
